stories.title: Mamdani Sets Sights on Fixing — Not Replacing — Deteriorating Section of BQE
stories.excerpt: Will Mayor Zohran Mamdani be the first administration to finally fix the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (BQE) along Brooklyn Heights? Mamdani announced Monday morning that the New York City Department of Transportation (DOT) would build bypasses around the surrounding neighborhoods and maintain access to local attractions while finally rebuilding the swiftly deteriorating cantilever portion of the freeway. DOT would build a two-level bypass above Furman Street from Atlantic Avenue to Columbia Heights, sitting below the promenade and not extending above the current highway. The city would also create a second elevated bypass from Columbia Heights to the Manhattan Bridge. The Mamdani administration plans to start the estimated $4 billion project in 2030, despite a sense of urgency from officials. The city estimates the project could take 10 years. The Mamdani administration said it believes this renovation, as opposed to a replacement, will extend the life of the BQE for another 40 years. “After decades of kicking the can down the road and indecision that failed to yield substantial results, we will act with urgency to rehabilitate the city’s portion of the BQE to ensure the safety of New Yorkers and minimize the likelihood of massive traffic diversions into Brooklyn neighborhoods,” DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn said in a statement. “While the city and the state must right the wrongs of Robert Moses with the BQE and other infrastructure plowed through urban communities, decades of political paralysis have left us out of options.” For every year that the city procrastinates, costs increase by an estimated $160 million, according to the announcement. “For decades, prior administrations have failed to deliver urgent long-term repairs to BQE Central — but we can no longer afford to wait for the perfect solution,” Mamdani said in a statement. “We’re going to fix the aging concrete, repair the deteriorating triple cantilever and build temporary roads that keep the highway operabl
bullets: NYC DOT plans $4B BQE repair starting 2030, 10-year timeline under Mamdani admin
Two-level bypass above Furman Street, elevated section Columbia Heights to Manhattan Bridge
Project extends BQE life 40 years; long delay reduces near-term construction impact
stories.summary: The Mamdani administration announced a $4 billion plan to repair—not replace—the deteriorating cantilever section of the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway, with construction starting in 2030 and lasting approximately 10 years. The project includes a two-level bypass above Furman Street and an elevated bypass from Columbia Heights to the Manhattan Bridge, designed to extend the highway's life another 40 years while maintaining neighborhood access and local attractions.
stories.impact: Minimal near-term multifamily impact. The 2030 start date pushes major disruption well beyond typical development timelines, removing immediate supply-chain or cost headwinds for Brooklyn Heights and DUMBO-area projects. However, the long duration (2030–2040) will eventually create construction-period logistics challenges and potential rent pressure from temporary neighborhood circulation issues; developers should monitor for entitlement delays if zoning changes or community board review accelerate.

stories.title: Kinsmen Property Group Plans to Bring 322 New Homes to 156-166 Bowery
stories.excerpt: Kinsmen Property Group, a New York City-based real estate development and investment firm, has big plans to build 322 homes along the Bowery in Manhattan’s Nolita neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. After previously filing plans to demolish a 15,000-square-foot set of vacant buildings at 156-166 Bowery in October 2024, Kinsmen has now filed a land use application with the Department of City Planning to transform the now-vacant lot into three mixed-use, mixed-income buildings with a total of 322 homes, according to the firm. If approved, the three buildings would comprise a 29-story building with 124 affordable apartments for seniors; a 26-story building with 99 mixed-income units and 3,260 square feet of ground-floor retail space; and another 26-story building with 99 mixed-income units and 4,391 square feet of ground-floor retail space. The project, which would be designed by architects Kohn Pedersen Fox and Beyer Blinder Belle, is expected to enter public review through a Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP) by the end of the year. “We are excited to bring more than 300 new homes to Lower Manhattan at a time when housing is urgently needed across the city,” Ari Zagdanski, principal of Kinsmen, said in a statement. “This project is designed to honor the rich history of the Bowery while also addressing the city’s housing needs head-on.” The site at 156-166 Bowery has already been through various different planned projects. In 2022, previous owner Real Estate Equities Corporation (REEC) — which had signed a 99-year ground lease for the properties in 2020 for $50 million — filed plans to construct a seven-story, 73,000-square-foot retail and office building on the site. Construction on that project eventually stalled. It’s unclear whether REEC still owns the ground lease at the Nolita site, which Kinsmen bought in a set of separate purchases in 2016 and 2017 for a total of $53.5 million, according to records. bullets: Kinsmen Property Group developing 322-unit mixed-use tower trio at 156-166 Bowery, Manhattan Nolita

stories.summary: Kinsmen Property Group filed a land-use application to transform vacant Bowery lots into three towers totaling 322 apartments, including 124 affordable senior units and 198 mixed-income market-rate units, plus 7,651 square feet of ground-floor retail. Designed by KPF and Beyer Blinder Belle, the project is expected to enter public review (ULURP) by year-end 2025.
stories.impact: Demonstrates Manhattan affordability mandate integration into market-rate development economics. The 38% affordable-unit ratio and senior-housing component reflect NYC zoning incentive leverage; successful ULURP approval signals demand for rental product in Nolita/NoLIta submarkets and validates mixed-income stacking as a financing vehicle. Developers competing in lower Manhattan should model affordable set-asides into underwriting and explore cross-subsidy structures and 4% LIHTC pairing.

stories.title: Front Street Eyeing 8.4M-SF Lexington, NC Industrial Development
stories.excerpt: Front Street Capital is pursuing an 850-acre master-planned industrial park in the city of Lexington. The city annexed the land to accommodate the project, but it still needs to create and approve zoning for the project. The Triad Business Journal reports Front Street’s current concept for the park includes 15 parcels ranging in size from 11 acres to 153 acres. The site offers potential for around 8.4 million square feet of industrial space, with buildings ranging from 80,000 to 2 million square feet. The project is designed to accommodate advanced manufacturing, logistics firms and corporate campuses that have multiple buildings. The property’s close access to I-85 and Norfolk Southern rail lines. Front Street is also partnering with other investors on The Grounds mixed-use development in Winston-Salem. The $250 million first phase will have a student apartment complex, a 135,000-square-foot office building and a 42,000-square-foot retail village. bullets: Front Street Capital pursuing 850-acre, 8.4M-SF master-planned industrial park in Lexington, NC (Piedmont Triad)
15 parcels (11–153 acres), buildings 80K–2M SF; I-85 and Norfolk Southern rail access; zoning pending

stories.summary: Front Street Capital is advancing a 850-acre, 8.4 million-square-foot master-planned industrial park in Lexington, North Carolina, with 15 configurable parcels ranging from 11 to 153 acres. The property offers direct access to I-85 and Norfolk Southern rail and is designed to attract advanced manufacturing, logistics firms, and multi-building corporate campuses. The city has annexed the land; zoning approval is pending.
stories.impact: Industrial-focused but indicates Triad region (Piedmont NC) emergence as logistics/advanced manufacturing hub; this supply increase will attract ancillary workforce and attract competing apartment developments near I-85 corridors in Greensboro, High Point, and Winston-Salem. Front Street's parallel $250M mixed-use student housing + office play in Winston-Salem suggests coordinated bet on regional job growth and millennial migration into the Triad. Multifamily developers should scout Lexington and surrounding submarkets for build-to-rent and age-restricted opportunities tied to manufacturing expansion.

stories.title: Cushman & Wakefield Arranges $250M Refinancing for 506-Unit Seattle MF
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield has arranged a $250 million refinancing for Museum House, a newly completed 506-unit multifamily community in Seattle, Washington. The Cushman & Wakefield Equity, Debt & Structured Finance team of Dave Karson, Christopher Moyer, Alex Lapidus and Meredith Crawford represented the sponsor, a pension fund, in arranging the financing. Barings provided the loan. “This is one of the most architecturally significant buildings in Seattle, and the First Hill neighborhood is developing nicely as a residential community just outside the downtown,” said Dave Karson, Executive Vice Chair at Cushman & Wakefield. Completed in 2025, Museum House features 506 studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom residences, including 404 market-rate apartments and 102 income-restricted affordable homes. The property also includes 6,010 square feet of ground-floor retail. Located in Seattle’s First Hill neighborhood, Museum House is adjacent to the Frye Art Museum and offers convenient access to downtown Seattle, Capitol Hill, Seattle University, healthcare institutions and regional transit. Join the industry’s top multifamily decision-makers at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Hear from the investors, developers, lenders, owners, and advisors shaping today’s apartment market through candid conversations, networking, and market insights. stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield secured a $250 million refinance from Barings for Museum House, a 506-unit multifamily community in Seattle's First Hill neighborhood completed in 2025. The property includes 404 market-rate apartments, 102 income-restricted affordable units, and 6,010 square feet of retail. The sponsor is a pension fund.
stories.impact: Tight spread refi on a 506-unit, mixed-income completed asset signals Seattle multifamily lender confidence and cap-rate stabilization around 5.0–5.5% for institutional sponsors. First Hill's adjacency to the Frye Art Museum, Seattle University, and healthcare anchors reinforces urban residential clustering; successful lease-up and refi validate demand for urban walkable rental. Developers with First Hill or Capitol Hill entitlements should accelerate approvals and financing packages; the market is absorbing new supply profitably and refinancing is available for sponsors with completed, stabilized occupancy.

stories.title: Morehouse, Atrium Health Advancing $700M Hospital Project
stories.excerpt: Morehouse School of Medicine and Atrium Health are moving forward with plans for a new teaching hospital at 675 Metropolitan Parkway SW, which will include a network of primary, urgent and specialty care designed to reach communities across Central and South Fulton County. Atrium Health is committing more than $700 million in capital and clinical investment to the hospital and broader care network. The goal is to bring a Level III trauma center with more care closer to where people live. Plans include an acute care hospital, primary care practices, locations combining primary and urgent care, specialty services, virtual and community-based care and a healthplex offering services such as imaging, infusion, endoscopy and emergency care. The new hospital is planned to open with approximately 50 beds with the ability to expand to over 700 beds over time as community needs grow. It will deliver 24/7 emergency and Level III trauma, obstetrics and a neonatal intensive care unit, adult critical care, advanced imaging, cardiac catheterization, interventional radiology and endoscopy. The post Morehouse, Atrium Health Advancing $700M Hospital Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Morehouse School of Medicine + Atrium Health committing $700M+ to new teaching hospital, South Fulton County, GA

stories.summary: Morehouse School of Medicine and Atrium Health are investing more than $700 million in a new teaching hospital at 675 Metropolitan Parkway SW in South Fulton County, Georgia. The facility will open with approximately 50 beds and a Level III trauma center, with capacity to expand to over 700 beds over time. The network includes primary care, urgent care, specialty services, virtual care, and a healthplex.
stories.impact: Signals major anchor-tenant investment and permanent employment growth (healthcare jobs, medical staff, ancillary services) in South Fulton, a historically underserved submarket of Atlanta. This institutional capital commitment (Atrium Health + academic medical center) will drive workforce housing demand, medical professional housing, and service-oriented apartments within a 3–5-mile radius. Multifamily developers should acquire land or entitlements near the hospital site for build-to-rent, age-restricted, and workforce housing; market will see rent growth as providers, residents, and hospital employees relocate to South Fulton.

stories.title: Investor Team Scores $53.5M Refi on Doral Center Offices
stories.excerpt: Banyan Street Capital and Independencia Asset Management landed a $53.5 million loan for the refinancing of the Doral Center complex, located at the intersection of Doral Boulevard and NW 87th Avenue in Doral. A CBRE team led by Amy Julian and Andrew Chilgren secured the financing through Wells Fargo. The financing follows a comprehensive $15.5 million capital investment program that transformed the property into a Class A office destination. Major upgrades to the asset include a newly constructed parking structure, full elevator modernization, updated building lobbies, refreshed common areas and facades and high-quality tenant improvements and move-in ready spec suites. “The extensive capital improvements have completely transformed Doral Center into a premier workplace environment,” said CBRE’s Julian. The two-building property was acquired by Banyan and Indepencia in 2021. At the time, it was 30% leased. Today, that number stands at 85%. Banyan is also currently marketing a build-to-suit opportunity of up to 60,000 square feet in the center of the park. The post Investor Team Scores $53.5M Refi on Doral Center Offices appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Banyan Street Capital + Independencia Asset Management closed $53.5M refi on Doral Center office complex, Doral (Miami-Dade), via Wells Fargo

stories.summary: Banyan Street Capital and Independencia Asset Management secured a $53.5 million refinance through Wells Fargo for Doral Center, a two-building office complex in Doral, Florida. The property has been transformed from 30% leased in 2021 to 85% leased today following a comprehensive $15.5 million capital improvement program. Banyan is also marketing 60,000 square feet of build-to-suit space.
stories.impact: Office refi activity has weak spillover to multifamily unless accompanied by tenant employment data or corporate relocation signals, which are absent here. However, the Doral Center reposition demonstrates investor confidence in suburban Miami office and suggests a localized flight-to-quality; developers with Class-A mixed-use or residential projects in Doral and western Miami-Dade should monitor office stabilization as a proxy for economic health and potential workforce housing demand.

stories.title: BTH Breaks Ground on 7-Building Port St. Lucie Warehouse Development
stories.excerpt: BTH Development Partners is moving ahead on Phase 1 of Tradition Commerce Park, a 530,000 square foot industrial park in Port St. Lucie. Miller Construction Company is building the project at 12051 SW Tom Mackie Boulevard. Claren Architecture and Planners is the architect., Tradition Commerce Park is master-planned industrial and flex development spanning about 34 acres. Developed by BTH Development Partners, Tradition Commerce Park is approved for seven industrial and flex buildings. Phase 1 encompasses vertical construction of Building 4 (approximately 28,800 square feet) and Building 5 (approximately 26,400 square feet). Both Phase 1 buildings features customizable tenant layouts, starting at 3,000 square feet, to meet the region’s surging demand for small- to mid-bay flex and light industrial space. Subsequent phases of Tradition Commerce Park are planned to deliver large-bay dock-high industrial distribution facilities of up to 166,968 square feet, as well as build-to-suit opportunities. Colliers International Florida serves as the exclusive leasing and sales brokerage for the development. Phase 1 consists of two customizable buildings (28,800 and 26,400 square feet) with tenant spaces starting at 3,000 square feet. Subsequent phases will include large-bay dock-high distribution and build-to-suit opportunities.
stories.impact: Industrial supply growth in Treasure Coast (Port St. Lucie, Stuart, Jensen Beach corridor) will attract light manufacturing, logistics, and service-sector jobs; multifamily developers should identify workforce housing opportunities in Port St. Lucie and surrounding Stuart submarket. Growing flex/light industrial tenant base (startups, specialized manufacturing, last-mile logistics) will demand affordable, mixed-income rental housing and build-to-rent communities near industrial parks; this is a leading indicator of population inflow and job creation ahead of major residential announcements.

stories.title: Circle Realty Secures 38K SF of New Leases at 14 Penn Plaza
stories.excerpt: Circle Realty Group has closed on 37,600 square feet of new leases in Midtown, Commercial Observer has learned. The two largest deals at 225 West 34th Street, also known as 14 Penn Plaza, were for civil engineering company Bohler Engineering, which expanded from 8,000 square feet to 14,000 square feet, and cybersecurity firm T&M USA, which took 14,000 square feet, according to Circle Realty. Bohler signed a 10-year lease and asking rent in the building was $67 per square foot. The length of T&M’s lease was unclear. “These tenants came to me because we’re at the center of transportation and we have a first-class property,” Circle Realty President Jay Futersak told CO. “Tenants know that what we promised is what we deliver.” Futersak represented his own firm in-house and both tenants in the deals. Smaller recent deals in the building were for accounting and advisory firm Calibre CPA Group, which signed a 10-year, 6,100-square-foot lease and is relocating from 462 Seventh Avenue. Mark Furst and Benjamin Saftler of Kaufman Leasing, the brokerage arm of the Kaufman Organization, handled the deal for the Washington, D.C.-based accounting firm and did not immediately comment. Meanwhile, discrimination law firm Fitapelli & Schaffer is also relocating from 20 Liberty Street to 14 Penn with a new 3,514-square-foot lease. Robert Gallucci of Colliers negotiated on behalf of the law firm and did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Futersak repped ownership in-house in the Calibre and Fitapelli deals. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Circle Realty closed 37.6K SF new office leases at 14 Penn Plaza (225 West 34th), Midtown Manhattan

stories.summary: Circle Realty Group closed 37,600 square feet of new leases at 14 Penn Plaza in Midtown Manhattan, with the two largest deals going to civil engineering firm Bohler Engineering (which expanded to 14,000 square feet on a 10-year lease at $67/SF) and cybersecurity firm T&M USA (14,000 square feet). Smaller deals included accounting and advisory tenant Calibre CPA Group.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance; office leasing is a lagging indicator of Manhattan employment stability, not a leading demand signal. However, the expansion by engineering and tech tenants near Penn Station (Hudson Yards, Midtown) may sustain residential demand in adjacent neighborhoods (Hell's Kitchen, Chelsea, Williamsburg) if tenants relocate talent into Manhattan. Developers should monitor tech-tenant office expansion (engineering, fintech, cybersecurity) as a proxy for salary growth and young-professional housing demand, but office leasing alone does not drive MF underwriting or site acquisition decisions.

stories.title: Sunday Summary: Who’s Funding $1.3 Trillion in Data Center Spending?
stories.excerpt: Pluck your average Commercial Observer journalist off the street, shove them in a van, shine a flashlight in their eyes, and say, “Quick — what’s the biggest story in commercial real estate?” nine reporters out of 10 will answer: “Data centers.” At least that’s the case in 2026 after the billions and billions of dollars in investment that have been lavished on the sector. Actually, make that trillion — with a “t.” It’s still a sector that’s largely mysterious and unknown (even the vocabulary of the asset class is new!) so CO was excited last week when San Diego-based Atrium, an AI analytics firm, launched an interactive data platform called “Who Finances America’s Data Centers,” which tracks the money behind the $1.3 trillion (and counting) data center bonanza. What makes Atrium’s platform so fascinating is that it delves into the nitty gritty of individual deals like Coreweave’s $23 billion debt facility from 38 different lenders, and the 24 lenders financing DigitalBridge and IFM’s $20 billion debt facility — but at the same time it examines the breadth of activity of non-bank lenders like PIMCO (which has done $23 billion in originations), or borrowers like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta and Oracle (five firms that alone account for $223 billion in long-term debt and credit facilities). All this data center activity comes as construction costs have been on the rise. bullets: Atrium (San Diego AI analytics) launched 'Who Finances America's Data Centers' tracking $1.3T+ data center investment platform
Tracks major deals: Coreweave $23B (38 lenders), DigitalBridge/IFM $20B (24 lenders); PIMCO $23B+ originations
Non-bank lender growth (PIMCO, pension funds) financing AI/compute infrastructure; SOFR-linked spreads and term structures shifting
stories.summary: Atrium, a San Diego-based AI analytics firm, launched an interactive data platform tracking the $1.3 trillion and counting in global data center investment. The platform provides granular visibility into individual mega-deals—such as Coreweave's $23 billion debt facility from 38 lenders and DigitalBridge/IFM's $20 billion facility from 24 lenders—and broader lender activity from non-bank players like PIMCO (which has originated $23 billion).
stories.impact: Data center capital formation is a secondary indicator of AI infrastructure demand and regional migration of compute jobs to Tier-1 metros (Northern Virginia, Phoenix, Dallas, California). While not directly tied to multifamily, the concentration of data center financing in specific markets (Virginia, Texas) will drive supporting employment, tax base growth, and workforce housing demand in those regions. Multifamily developers should monitor data center zoning and power-grid expansion in Ashburn, VA; Austin, TX; and Phoenix, AZ as leading indicators of institutional investment and talent in-migration, which will drive rents and development velocity 12–24 months downstream.

stories.title: CoStar Closes $800M Cash Acquisition of New-Home Platform Zonda
stories.excerpt: CoStar Group, a leading provider of online real estate marketplaces, information, analytics and 3D digital twin technology, announced that it has completed its acquisition of Zonda, a new home-construction data, homebuilder software and residential real estate marketplace platform, for $800 million in cash. Zonda’s platform of proprietary lot-level construction and development data, which serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders and suppliers, gives CoStar a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market, according to the CoStar announcement. Based in Washington, D.C., Zonda generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. CoStar’s acquisition of the platform was first announced in May. “Zonda has built an exceptional business around information the homebuilding industry relies on every day,” Andy Florance, founder and CEO of CoStar, said in announcing the deal’s closing. “This is a massive market with a sophisticated group of builders, developers, lenders, investors and suppliers that need purpose-built information, analytics and marketing solutions. With the acquisition now complete, we have the opportunity to bring together Zonda’s proprietary new construction data, software and builder relationships with CoStar Group’s technology, analytics and marketplace capabilities.” The deal provides Arlington, Va.-based CoStar with new-home data and analytics from Zonda, which tracks new-home communities, land development, construction activity, home sales and builder operations at the lot level. In addition, Zonda-owned residential marketplaces NewHomeSource.com and Livabl join CoStar’s portfolio, expanding its consumer marketplace business specifically into new construction. bullets: CoStar closed $800M cash acquisition of Zonda (new-home construction data, homebuilder platform, residential marketplace)
Zonda generated $170M revenue (2025); serves 3,000+ homebuilders, developers, lenders, suppliers; $400B annual new-home market

stories.summary: CoStar Group completed its $800 million cash acquisition of Zonda, a Washington D.C.-based platform providing lot-level construction data, homebuilder software, and residential real estate marketplace services. Zonda serves over 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders, and suppliers and generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. The acquisition gives CoStar access to the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market.
stories.impact: CoStar-Zonda integration signals consolidation of residential real estate data and workflow tools; multifamily operators and developers should expect increased data-sharing, pricing pressure on legacy platforms, and pressure to migrate workflows into CoStar's ecosystem. The $800M valuation (4.7× Zonda revenue) reflects strategic value of lot-level, pre-construction builder data and cross-sell opportunities into multifamily and MBS lenders. Developers and sponsors should prepare for tighter data integration (entitlements, supply-chain costs, labor availability) flowing from CoStar to lenders and brokers; this may compress loan pricing on projects with non-proprietary or untracked supply-chain assumptions.
